# The intranet must reduce attention cost before employees can trust it as the information home

**Insight:** Employees and content owners do not only need more information in the intranet. They need lower effort to notice, find, revisit, and trust the right information at the right time.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Search and navigation gaps prevent reliable self-service information access]], [[Important updates lose visibility across news and parallel channels]], [[Distributed content ownership makes freshness fragile]], [[Intranet migration needs active content selection and legacy-source retirement]]

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> Die häufigste Rückmeldung, die ich, seit ich bei People bin, bekommen habe, ist, wir wissen, dass wir viel Angebote beim Thema Beruf und Familie haben, wir finden es nicht. Wir finden es nicht. - P02
>
> Translation: The most frequent feedback I have received since I have been in People is that we know there are many offers around Beruf und Familie, but we do not find them. We do not find them.

> Wir haben unterschiedlichste Lösungen wie Viva Engage und ich habe schon irgendwie höre viel, dass das langsam überfordert bei Informationen auf Viva Engage, auf Teams im Intranet zu finden sind und schön wäre es natürlich, wenn wir eine Lösung haben, die alles bietet um dort auch eben dieses. - P01
>
> Translation: There are very different solutions such as Viva Engage, and I already hear a lot that it is slowly overwhelming when information can be found on Viva Engage, on Teams, in the intranet, and of course it would be nice if there were one solution that offers everything there.

> Also selbst ich wo ich 18 Jahre im Konzern bin, weiß manchmal nicht wo welches Thema bei wem liegt. - P03
>
> Translation: Even I, who have been in the group for 18 years, sometimes do not know where which topic sits with whom.

> Idealerweise hätte mir das Intranet gesagt, Hey, die Region Europa hat sich neu strukturiert und da gibt es eine coole Präsentation dazu. Ich habe ein halbes Jahr später die selber aktiv aus dem Intranet rausgetaucht. - P04
>
> Translation: Ideally, the intranet would have told me, hey, the Europe region has been restructured and there is a good presentation about it. I actively pulled it out of the intranet myself half a year later.

> Für Ordnung also alles einfach ist ordentlich alles. Sortiert man weiß, wo man die Sachen findet. Es ist übersichtlich, aber es fehlen auch keine Informationen. - P05
>
> Translation: For order, so everything is simply orderly, everything is sorted, one knows where to find things. It is clear, but no information is missing.

> Die Ergebnisse sind dann meist auch so nicht gut in der Trefferliste sozusagen sortiert, sondern muss man schon wirklich auch immer gucken, das ist jetzt genau der, der der Link, den man eigentlich braucht. - P06
>
> Translation: The results are usually not well sorted in the hit list, so one really always has to check whether this is exactly the link one actually needs.

> Wenn man einfach das spiegelt und rüberzieht, dann ist es ja auch nicht geholfen, weil dann haben wir eigentlich den gleichen Sumpf nur auf einer anderen Plattform. - P07
>
> Translation: If one simply mirrors it and pulls it over, that does not help either, because then we basically have the same mess only on another platform.

> Ja, most Imports and II think we go that get the content right. Ja and like move away from this ding of sing as a document library like mics of teams can do that and c as a communication tool and ja, and and like this personal hub. - P08

**Business Impact:** Important employee information may not reach employees even when content owners publish and maintain it. Employees may also contact the wrong people or rely on private workarounds.
**Design Implication:** The intranet experience must make relevant content visible, retrievable, persistent, structured, accountable, and deliberately migrated without requiring users to monitor every channel, know the owning structure, or relearn each local page model.

## Recommendation
**Recommendation:** The new intranet should prioritize topic-based information access through connected search, persistent topic surfaces, and named accountable contacts before using personalization as the main discovery model.
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Search distrust shifts information seeking to personal contacts]], [[Channel fragmentation increases information load]], [[Static news structures hide enduring division topics]], [[Topic experts are hard to find from names and job titles alone]], [[Intranet and service portals do not provide a clear route to action]], [[New starters lack one orientation path to terms, people, and company context]], [[Intranet and SharePoint transitions break orientation continuity]], [[Compressed intranet migration risks content loss and shadow sources]]
**Expected Effect:** Users should need less personal memory, organizational knowledge, channel monitoring, system-boundary interpretation, onboarding guesswork, migration-specific relearning, and SharePoint-specific relearning to find current information, responsible experts, and next actions.
**Risk:** Evidence now includes a global business-development user, a global marketing trainee, an information technology stakeholder, a Talent Acquisition content owner, and a United Kingdom sales and marketing stakeholder. Field staff, frequent service-request users, employees in mainland China, regional intranet owners, and content owners with large migration workloads may need different entry points, performance models, mobile governance, or cutover support.
**Priority:** Medium

## Reference
When evidence is thin, do not create an insight; record the gap in [[SOP-Analysis-Process]]. Recommendations live inside their anchor insight and are also listed in [[_recommendations-register]].

notes.body:
# Persistent utility entry points create low-effort intranet visits

**Threshold check:** P01, P02, P05, and P07 directly support this pattern.
**Theme (if related to one):** [[Important updates lose visibility across news and parallel channels]]
**Process Phase:** Communication Consumption
**Description:** Persistent utility areas such as the bulletin board, canteen information, seasonal actions, and repeated workday forms create recognizable low-effort reasons to open the intranet.
**Why it works:** The entry points stay visible and do not require users to understand deep navigation.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** Employees may lose familiar reasons to check the intranet and may rely more on informal channels.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 5
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P05, P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> Und dort sind bei den Kollegen tatsächlich auch, also ist sicherlich keine empirische Studie, ich kann nur aus Ausschnitten. Berichten, die ich höre, aber dort sind im Internet die relevantesten Kanäle, das schwarze Brett. - P01
>
> Translation: And for colleagues there, although this is certainly not an empirical study and I can only report from excerpts that I hear, the most relevant channels in the intranet are the bulletin board.

> Das schwarze Brett finde ich großartig. Ich liebe es, ich finde es auch gut, das ist unauffällig und dennoch sieht man es, ehrlich gesagt vergesse ich es meistens und wenn ich dann was im Intranet zu tun habe, dann ach ja, guck mal ins Schwarze Brett könntest du auch mal wieder gucken, finde ich es super, das ist was was wo ich ganz ehrlich sagen muss das das ist so unkompliziert unauffällig aber dennoch total ist eine gute Sache ich finde es ich finde es super. - P02
>
> Translation: I think the bulletin board is great. I love it, I also think it is good, it is unobtrusive and yet one sees it; honestly I usually forget it, and when I then have something to do in the intranet, I think, ah yes, look at the bulletin board again, I think it is great, that is something where I honestly have to say that it is so uncomplicated and unobtrusive but still really a good thing, I think it is great.

> Ja, ja, aber es kann natürlich sein, dass ich es dann tatsächlich einmal nicht schaffe. Und dann mache ich am übernächsten Tag 2 Türchen auf, aber da nutze ich es dann oft ja. - P02
>
> Translation: Yes, yes, but of course it can happen that I actually do not manage it once. And then I open two doors the day after next, but then I often use it, yes.

> Also in Singapur war da auch so in der Weihnachtszeit ne Sache, ich weiß nicht ob das auch bei anderen Locations so war, aber da gab es so nen kleinen Adventskalender und das fand ich auch irgendwie süß wo man so jeden Tag dann irgendwie sich gefreut hat. - P05
>
> Translation: In Singapore there was also something at Christmas time, I do not know whether it was also at other locations, but there was a small Advent calendar and I somehow found that nice, where every day one somehow looked forward to it.

> Also Dinge die ich ab und zu tun muss, aber dann schon noch mal den Link brauch. - P07
>
> Translation: Things that I have to do from time to time, but where I then still need the link again.

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 6b. Positive patterns use the same dedup and evidence standards as pain points and must be supported by at least two distinct interviews. Do not fold them into pain points or insights; keep them visible as their own category.

notes.body:
# SharePoint pages make content maintenance easier to scan and update

**Threshold check:** P01, P02, and P03 directly support this pattern.
**Theme (if related to one):** [[]]
**Process Phase:** Content Publishing
**Description:** Content owners perceive SharePoint pages as easier to structure, maintain, and scan than the current intranet authoring experience.
**Why it works:** The page structure appears more modern and direct to edit.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** A new intranet could lose a clear source of confidence for content owners if it does not preserve simple SharePoint-style authoring.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 4
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03

**Representative Quotes:**
> Wenn ich meine Artikel parallel in sharepoint einfach nur für mich um irgendwie eine schöne gedankliche Struktur aufzubauen, habe ich das in 2 Minuten ein wunderbares Layout erschaffen, über das ich mich sehr freue und ich sitze zur selben Zeit eine halbe Stunde manchmal im Intranet, um einen Artikel reinzustellen, auch mit langen Ladung Ladezeiten genau und habe im Backout. - P01
>
> Translation: When I create my articles in parallel in SharePoint just for myself to build a nice mental structure, I have created a wonderful layout in two minutes that I am very happy about, and at the same time I sometimes sit in the intranet for half an hour to post an article, also with long loading times, exactly, and I have in the backup.

> Also ich hab mich schon näher damit beschäftigt, ich hab ein paar Kolleginnen, die das. Tun im gleichen Bereich also meine Kollegin, die die Gesundheitsthemen macht, die hatten Sharepoint und ich glaube, es ist in der Pflege einfacher. - P02
>
> Translation: I have already looked into it more closely, and I have a few colleagues who do that in the same area; my colleague who handles health topics has SharePoint, and I think it is easier to maintain.

> Ich finde nicht schön, ist ansprechend, ist modern, ja ist ist irgendwie übersichtlich, klar ist es jetzt wieder viel Information, aber ja wenn ich dann wenn wenn ich dann hier mal in die Policies reingehe das ist dann ich weiß es nicht, es ist einfach viel also es ist viel. Viel einfacher. - P02
>
> Translation: I do not find it beautiful, it is appealing, it is modern, yes, it is somehow clear; of course it is again a lot of information, but yes, when I then go into the policies, I do not know, it is simply a lot, so it is much easier.

> Ja, das sharepoint Tool ist ja ganz cool da zum zum zum Bauen. Also dass es vernetzt ist und relativ selbsterklärend zu bedienen ist. Also vom Content Management System her finde ich jetzt im Vergleich zum Internet deutlich akzeptabler. - P03
>
> Translation: Yes, the SharePoint tool is quite cool for building. That it is connected and relatively self-explanatory to use. From the content management system perspective, I find it clearly more acceptable compared with the intranet.

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 6b. Positive patterns use the same dedup and evidence standards as pain points and must be supported by at least two distinct interviews. Do not fold them into pain points or insights; keep them visible as their own category.

> Translation: When I create my articles in parallel in SharePoint just for myself to build a nice mental structure, I have created a wonderful layout in two minutes that I am very happy about, and at the same time I sometimes sit in the intranet for half an hour to post an article, also with long loading times, exactly, and I have in the backup.

> Also ich hab mich schon näher damit beschäftigt, ich hab ein paar Kolleginnen, die das. Tun im gleichen Bereich also meine Kollegin, die die Gesundheitsthemen macht, die hatten Sharepoint und ich glaube, es ist in der Pflege einfacher. - P02
>
> Translation: I have already looked into it more closely, and I have a few colleagues who do that in the same area; my colleague who handles health topics has SharePoint, and I think it is easier to maintain.

> Ich finde nicht schön, ist ansprechend, ist modern, ja ist ist irgendwie übersichtlich, klar ist es jetzt wieder viel Information, aber ja wenn ich dann wenn wenn ich dann hier mal in die Policies reingehe das ist dann ich weiß es nicht, es ist einfach viel also es ist viel. Viel einfacher. - P02
>
> Translation: I do not find it beautiful, it is appealing, it is modern, yes, it is somehow clear; of course it is again a lot of information, but yes, when I then go into the policies, I do not know, it is simply a lot, so it is much easier.

> Ja, das sharepoint Tool ist ja ganz cool da zum zum zum Bauen. Also dass es vernetzt ist und relativ selbsterklärend zu bedienen ist. Also vom Content Management System her finde ich jetzt im Vergleich zum Internet deutlich akzeptabler. - P03
>
> Translation: Yes, the SharePoint tool is quite cool for building. That it is connected and relatively self-explanatory to use. From the content management system perspective, I find it clearly more acceptable compared with the intranet.

# Content owners balancing publishing and findability

**Before completing:** P01, P02, P03, and P07 form a consistent content-owner segment. The segment should be split later if governance scope, publishing rights, audience responsibility, or service-intake ownership create different solution needs.

**Segment:** Content owners who publish, maintain, or structure employee-facing intranet information.
**Based on Interviews:** [[P01]], [[P02]], [[P03]], [[P07]]

## Context
Content owners maintain division, wellbeing, sustainability, Talent Acquisition, or corporate communication pages. They use the intranet to publish news, benefits, policies, contacts, background information, or service entry points. They often know internal structures better than ordinary employees.

## Goals
Content owners need published information to remain findable, current, and visible after the first news moment. They need authoring and governance models that reduce duplicate posting and manual rescue work.
P07 adds a service-owner variation. Talent Acquisition content must serve employees and managers, and migration work may require separate stakeholder communication.

## Related Themes
- [[Search and navigation gaps prevent reliable self-service information access]]
- [[Important updates lose visibility across news and parallel channels]]
- [[Distributed content ownership makes freshness fragile]]

## Related Pain Points
- [[Search distrust shifts information seeking to personal contacts]]
- [[Topic experts are hard to find from names and job titles alone]]
- [[Distributed ownership leaves intranet content stale]]
- [[Channel fragmentation increases information load]]
- [[Static news structures hide enduring division topics]]
- [[Intranet and service portals do not provide a clear route to action]]
- [[Compressed intranet migration risks content loss and shadow sources]]

## Related Needs
- [[Users need reliable paths to role-relevant information]]
- [[Content owners need governed channels that keep important updates visible]]
- [[Users need topic-based expert discovery]]

# Proto-Segments

| Interview ID | Suspected segment | Key characteristics | Persona decision | Next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | Internal communications content owner | Publishes division news, rebuilds intranet pages, monitors global news, needs reliable authoring, media handling, mobile reach, and content governance. | No persona note. Fewer than three matching interviews. | Compare with future content owners and field employees. |
| P02 | Wellbeing content owner and long-tenured intranet user | Maintains Beruf und Familie content, uses favorites and multiple channels, needs reliable search, navigation, bilingual local publishing, and governed visibility for employee offers. | No persona note. Fewer than three matching interviews. | Compare with future content owners and long-tenured non-owner users. |
| P03 | Sustainability communications owner and long-tenured intranet user | Builds sustainability SharePoint, uses intranet several times daily, needs topic-based search, current contacts, cross-SharePoint discovery, and mobile access for non-desk employees. | Created [[Content owners balancing publishing and findability]]. | Check whether future content owners split by publishing rights or audience scope. |
| P04 | Global Academy business-development user | Supports international Academy growth, uses intranet weekly, needs management updates, country and business data, training information, topic experts, and clearer routes between intranet and service portals. | No persona note. First clear international business-development segment. | Compare with future international knowledge workers and Academy users. |
| P05 | Global marketing trainee and intern | Works across Spanish regional marketing and global branding, uses intranet once or twice weekly, relies on Binder and SharePoint folders, needs onboarding terms, people context, local/global news, and clearer navigation. | No persona note. First clear trainee segment. | Compare with future trainees, interns, and new starters. |
| P06 | Long-tenured information technology and North Asia stakeholder | Uses the global intranet daily, knows search terms through tenure, monitors news and management information, and needs consistent SharePoint transitions, global performance, China availability, and mobile governance. | No persona note. First clear information technology governance stakeholder segment. | Compare with future technical stakeholders and regional leaders. |
| P07 | Talent Acquisition content owner and People services user | Maintains recruiting and employer-branding information, uses intranet content for employee and manager audiences, needs migration lead time, consistent templates, service-entry continuity, and findable People information. | Extended [[Content owners balancing publishing and findability]]. | Check whether People service owners split from communication content owners because they manage service-intake workflows as well as information pages. |
| P08 | United Kingdom sales and marketing stakeholder | Uses the intranet rarely, relies on Teams for current work content, sees the United Kingdom intranet as a legacy link library, and expects a future intranet to become a relevant work-life hub and company town square. | No persona note. First clear United Kingdom Teams-led low-intranet-use segment. | Compare with future regional knowledge workers and sales or marketing stakeholders. |
